R4E-C008: The company acquired British Columbia Steamship Company Inc., a separate Washington corporation, on 15 May 1975. Qualification: Keep the federal Canadian company and Washington company as distinct legal entities.

R4E-C009: The company states that its share capital is held by five directors in right of the Province; the balance sheet lists five issued common shares. R4E-C012: The original Act requires at least eight directors, appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council from persons holding elected municipal office.

R4E-C016: The same 1982 amendment adds the express Crown-agent provision to the authority’s establishing section. Qualification: This claim concerns the express statutory agency clause, not a claim that no other Crown relationship existed before this date.

R4E-C019: The 1985 amendment’s new BC Transit Act section 2.1 transfers all MTOC property and rights to BC Transit and makes BC Transit liable for MTOC debts and obligations. The provision commenced on 1 June 1985. Qualification: A transfer/assumption event. The provision does not itself declare MTOC dissolved.

R4E-C021: OIC 1096/1985 appoints nine MTOC directors and its chair effective 1 June 1985, while OIC 1095 appoints the BC Transit board. Qualification: This is affirmative evidence against automatically treating the 1985 asset transfer as MTOC legal dissolution. Its ultimate legal end remains unproved.
